passages.text: A man who remains stiff-necked after much reproof will suddenly be shattered beyond recovery.
passages.sermon:
A man receives many warnings.
This man refuses to listen.
He is stubborn.
He does not change his ways.
Suddenly, he will be broken.
No one can heal him.
passages.original: אִ֣ישׁ תּ֭וֹכָחוֹת מַקְשֶׁה־ עֹ֑רֶף פֶּ֥תַע יִ֝שָּׁבֵ֗ר וְאֵ֣ין מַרְפֵּֽא׃

passages.text: When the righteous flourish, the people rejoice, but when the wicked rule, the people groan.
passages.sermon:
Righteous people help a community.
When many righteous people live in a place, the people feel joy.
The people rejoice because of the presence of the righteous.
Wicked people harm a community.
When a wicked person rules, the people suffer.
The people groan under the rule of the wicked.
passages.original: בִּרְב֣וֹת צַ֭דִּיקִים יִשְׂמַ֣ח הָעָ֑ם וּבִמְשֹׁ֥ל רָ֝שָׁ֗ע יֵאָ֥נַֽח עָֽם׃

passages.text: A man who loves wisdom brings joy to his father, but a companion of prostitutes squanders his wealth.
passages.sermon:
A man loves wisdom.
This man brings joy to his father.
A man spends time with prostitutes.
This man loses his wealth.
passages.original: אִֽישׁ־ אֹהֵ֣ב חָ֭כְמָה יְשַׂמַּ֣ח אָבִ֑יו וְרֹעֶ֥ה ז֝וֹנ֗וֹת יְאַבֶּד־ הֽוֹן׃

passages.text: By justice a king brings stability to the land, but a man who exacts tribute demolishes it.
passages.sermon:
A king rules a land.
A just king brings stability to the land.
He uses justice to make the land strong.
A man who takes tribute from others harms the land.
He destroys the land by demanding payments.
passages.original: מֶ֗לֶךְ בְּ֭מִשְׁפָּט יַעֲמִ֣יד אָ֑רֶץ וְאִ֖ישׁ תְּרוּמ֣וֹת יֶֽהֶרְסֶֽנָּה׃

passages.text: A man who flatters his neighbor spreads a net for his feet.
passages.sermon:
A man flatters his neighbor.
He uses smooth and insincere words.
He spreads a net for his neighbor’s feet.
He sets a trap for his neighbor.
passages.original: גֶּ֭בֶר מַחֲלִ֣יק עַל־ רֵעֵ֑הוּ רֶ֝֗שֶׁת פּוֹרֵ֥שׂ עַל־ פְּעָמָֽיו׃

passages.text: An evil man is caught by his own sin, but a righteous one sings and rejoices.
passages.sermon:
An evil man commits sin.
His own sin traps him.
A righteous person lives rightly.
The righteous person sings.
The righteous person rejoices.
passages.original: בְּפֶ֤שַֽׁע אִ֣ישׁ רָ֣ע מוֹקֵ֑שׁ וְ֝צַדִּ֗יק יָר֥וּן וְשָׂמֵֽחַ׃

passages.text: The righteous consider the cause of the poor, but the wicked have no regard for such concerns.
passages.sermon:
A righteous person understands the needs of the poor.
A righteous person cares about justice for the poor.
A wicked person does not understand these things.
A wicked person does not care about the needs of the poor.
passages.original: יֹדֵ֣עַ צַ֭דִּיק דִּ֣ין דַּלִּ֑ים רָ֝שָׁ֗ע לֹא־ יָבִ֥ין דָּֽעַת׃

passages.text: Mockers inflame a city, but the wise turn away anger.
passages.sermon:
Mockers cause trouble in a city.
They stir up conflict.
Wise people calm anger.
They bring peace.
passages.original: אַנְשֵׁ֣י לָ֭צוֹן יָפִ֣יחוּ קִרְיָ֑ה וַ֝חֲכָמִ֗ים יָשִׁ֥יבוּ אָֽף׃

passages.text: If a wise man goes to court with a fool, there will be raving and laughing with no resolution.
passages.sermon:
A wise man may go to court with a fool.
The wise man uses good judgment.
The fool does not act with understanding.
The fool rages and laughs.
There is no peace or resolution in the dispute.
passages.original: אִֽישׁ־ חָכָ֗ם נִ֭שְׁפָּט אֶת־ אִ֣ישׁ אֱוִ֑יל וְרָגַ֥ז וְ֝שָׂחַ֗ק וְאֵ֣ין נָֽחַת׃

passages.text: Men of bloodshed hate a blameless man, but the upright care for his life.
passages.sermon: Men of bloodshed hate a blameless man.\r\nUpright people care for the blameless man’s life.
passages.original: אַנְשֵׁ֣י דָ֭מִים יִשְׂנְאוּ־ תָ֑ם וִֽ֝ישָׁרִ֗ים יְבַקְשׁ֥וּ נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃

passages.text: A fool vents all his anger, but a wise man holds it back.
passages.sermon:
A fool speaks out all his anger.
A fool does not hold back his feelings.
A wise man controls his anger.
A wise man keeps his feelings inside.
A wise man does not speak out in anger.
passages.original: כָּל־ ר֭וּחוֹ יוֹצִ֣יא כְסִ֑יל וְ֝חָכָ֗ם בְּאָח֥וֹר יְשַׁבְּחֶֽנָּה׃

passages.text: If a ruler listens to lies, all his officials will be wicked.
passages.sermon:
A ruler holds authority over others.
A ruler can choose what to believe.
If a ruler listens to lies, he accepts falsehood.
When a ruler accepts falsehood, he encourages evil.
All his officials will become wicked.
passages.original: מֹ֭שֵׁל מַקְשִׁ֣יב עַל־ דְּבַר־ שָׁ֑קֶר כָּֽל־ מְשָׁרְתָ֥יו רְשָׁעִֽים׃

passages.text: The poor man and the oppressor have this in common: The LORD gives light to the eyes of both.
passages.sermon:
The poor man and the oppressor meet.
The LORD gives light to the eyes of both.
God gives understanding to both the poor and the oppressor.
God is the source of wisdom for every person.
passages.original: רָ֤שׁ וְאִ֣ישׁ תְּכָכִ֣ים נִפְגָּ֑שׁוּ מֵ֤אִיר־ עֵינֵ֖י שְׁנֵיהֶ֣ם יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: A king who judges the poor with fairness— his throne will be established forever.
passages.sermon:
A king rules over his people.
This king judges poor people.
He judges them with fairness.
He treats them justly.
God will make this king’s throne secure.
His throne will last forever.
passages.original: מֶ֤לֶךְ שׁוֹפֵ֣ט בֶּֽאֱמֶ֣ת דַּלִּ֑ים כִּ֝סְא֗וֹ לָעַ֥ד יִכּֽוֹן׃

passages.text: A rod of correction imparts wisdom, but a child left to himself disgraces his mother.
passages.sermon: A rod of correction gives wisdom.\r\nA child needs guidance.\r\nIf a child has no guidance, he brings shame to his mother.
passages.original: שֵׁ֣בֶט וְ֭תוֹכַחַת יִתֵּ֣ן חָכְמָ֑ה וְנַ֥עַר מְ֝שֻׁלָּ֗ח מֵבִ֥ישׁ אִמּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: When the wicked thrive, rebellion increases; but the righteous will see their downfall.
passages.sermon:
Wicked people can thrive in a community.
When wicked people thrive, rebellion increases.
Righteous people live among the wicked.
Righteous people will see the downfall of the wicked.
passages.original: בִּרְב֣וֹת רְ֭שָׁעִים יִרְבֶּה־ פָּ֑שַׁע וְ֝צַדִּיקִ֗ים בְּֽמַפַּלְתָּ֥ם יִרְאֽוּ׃

passages.text: Discipline your son, and he will give you rest; he will bring delight to your soul.
passages.sermon: A father must discipline his son.\r\nA disciplined son will give his father rest.\r\nA disciplined son will bring delight to his father’s soul.
passages.original: יַסֵּ֣ר בִּ֭נְךָ וִֽינִיחֶ֑ךָ וְיִתֵּ֖ן מַעֲדַנִּ֣ים לְנַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃פ

passages.text: Where there is no vision, the people cast off restraint; but blessed is he who keeps the Law.
passages.sermon:
When there is no vision, people lose self-control.
People act without restraint.
A person who keeps God's Law is blessed.
Obeying God's Law brings happiness.
passages.original: בְּאֵ֣ין חָ֭זוֹן יִפָּ֣רַֽע עָ֑ם וְשֹׁמֵ֖ר תּוֹרָ֣ה אַשְׁרֵֽהוּ׃

passages.text: A servant cannot be corrected by words alone; though he understands, he will not respond.
passages.sermon:
A servant is a person under authority.
Words alone cannot correct a servant.
The servant may understand the words.
But he will not respond.
passages.original: בִּ֭דְבָרִים לֹא־ יִוָּ֣סֶר עָ֑בֶד כִּֽי־ יָ֝בִ֗ין וְאֵ֣ין מַעֲנֶֽה׃

passages.text: Do you see a man who speaks in haste? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
passages.sermon:
A man speaks quickly and without thinking.
He does not wait or consider his words.
You see this man.
A fool is someone who lacks wisdom.
There is more hope for a fool than for the man who speaks in haste.
passages.original: חָזִ֗יתָ אִ֭ישׁ אָ֣ץ בִּדְבָרָ֑יו תִּקְוָ֖ה לִכְסִ֣יל מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: A servant pampered from his youth will bring grief in the end.
passages.sermon:
A servant is a person who serves another.
If you pamper a servant from his youth, you give him too much comfort and indulgence.
This servant grows up without discipline.
In the end, this servant will bring grief.
Pampering a servant from childhood leads to sorrow later.
passages.original: מְפַנֵּ֣ק מִנֹּ֣עַר עַבְדּ֑וֹ וְ֝אַחֲרִית֗וֹ יִהְיֶ֥ה מָנֽוֹן׃

passages.text: An angry man stirs up dissension, and a hot-tempered man abounds in transgression.
passages.sermon: An angry man causes conflict.\r\nA hot-tempered man commits many sins.
passages.original: אִֽישׁ־ אַ֭ף יְגָרֶ֣ה מָד֑וֹן וּבַ֖עַל חֵמָ֣ה רַב־ פָּֽשַׁע׃

passages.text: A man’s pride will bring him low, but a humble spirit will obtain honor.
passages.sermon:
Pride brings a man down.
A proud person falls.
A humble person receives honor.
A person with a humble spirit gains respect.
passages.original: גַּאֲוַ֣ת אָ֭דָם תַּשְׁפִּילֶ֑נּוּ וּשְׁפַל־ ר֝֗וּחַ יִתְמֹ֥ךְ כָּבֽוֹד׃

passages.text: A partner to a thief hates his own soul; he receives the oath, but does not testify.
passages.sermon:
A person who joins with a thief acts against himself.
He hears the oath in court.
He does not speak the truth.
He does not testify.
passages.original: חוֹלֵ֣ק עִם־ גַּ֭נָּב שׂוֹנֵ֣א נַפְשׁ֑וֹ אָלָ֥ה יִ֝שְׁמַ֗ע וְלֹ֣א יַגִּֽיד׃

passages.text: The fear of man is a snare, but whoever trusts in the LORD is set securely on high.
passages.sermon:
Fear of people traps a person.
This fear acts like a snare.
Trust in the LORD keeps a person safe.
The LORD lifts up those who trust Him.
Trust in the LORD gives security.
passages.original: חֶרְדַּ֣ת אָ֭דָם יִתֵּ֣ן מוֹקֵ֑שׁ וּבוֹטֵ֖חַ בַּיהוָ֣ה יְשֻׂגָּֽב׃

passages.text: Many seek the ruler’s favor, but a man receives justice from the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Many people want the ruler to show them favor.
They go to the ruler for help.
But true justice comes from the LORD.
The LORD gives each person what is right.
No one else can give true justice except the LORD.
passages.original: רַ֭בִּים מְבַקְשִׁ֣ים פְּנֵי־ מוֹשֵׁ֑ל וּ֝מֵיְהוָ֗ה מִשְׁפַּט־ אִֽישׁ׃

passages.text: An unjust man is detestable to the righteous, and one whose way is upright is detestable to the wicked.
passages.sermon:
Righteous people hate unjust people.
Unjust people do evil things.
Wicked people hate those who live upright lives.
Upright people do what is right.
passages.original: תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת צַ֭דִּיקִים אִ֣ישׁ עָ֑וֶל וְתוֹעֲבַ֖ת רָשָׁ֣ע יְשַׁר־ דָּֽרֶךְ׃פ
